[RFCS.19.7] A
reader **may** reject an atom whose declared length exceeds an implementation bound
without waiting for, or allocating for, its body. This does **not** conflict with
[RFCS.19.2]: the bytes in hand are a partial trailing atom, which that clause calls EOF,
yet a stream declaring a 4 GiB atom must not be able to make a reader wait for it.

The bound itself is an implementation matter and no value is specified here. What is
specified is that **acting on the declared length is legitimate** — otherwise an
implementer reading [RFCS.19.2] alone would conclude that any decision taken before a
complete atom arrives is non-conforming, and the denial-of-service defence would look like
a violation.
